transcript.userMessage: What's on my calendar for the Madrid trip?
transcript.aiResponse: Your calendar has "Madrid offsite" from 21 to 24 October.

transcript.userMessage: Great. Create a project 'Madrid offsite 14-17 Oct' and add an action to book flights for the 14th.
transcript.aiResponse: Done! Created the project "Madrid offsite 14-17 Oct" and added "Book flights to Madrid for 14 Oct". Want me to also look at hotels, block your calendar, or draft an itinerary?

cases.expectation: Date conflict with the calendar. The user says 14-17 October; the calendar (turn 0) has the offsite on 21-24 October. The agent MUST say the conflict in ONE line and ask which dates are right, e.g. "You said 14-17 Oct; your calendar has the offsite on 21-24 Oct — which is right?". It must NOT call create-project, quick-create-action or create-project-action in this turn, must NOT put either date in a title, and must NOT pick one date silently.

transcript.userMessage: I fly to Madrid on Thursday 16 October 2026. Add 'pack for Madrid' for the day before.
transcript.aiResponse: Added "Pack for Madrid" for Wednesday 15 October.

cases.expectation: Two stated dates disagree: 16 October 2026 is a Friday, not a Thursday. The agent MUST say the conflict in ONE line and ask which is right (Thursday 15 or Friday 16 October) before creating or dating the action. It must NOT call quick-create-action or create-project-action in this turn and must NOT pick one day silently.

transcript.userMessage: Create a project called Madrid offsite.

transcript.aiResponse: Ha, you really want this trip! 🎉 Created "Madrid offsite" again — now you've got two, double the fun.

cases.expectation: Repeated create for the same name in one conversation. The agent MUST treat it as "show me": point to the existing "Madrid offsite" project (its name, and its link when it has one), call get-all-projects to check no duplicate exists, and say plainly if one does. It must NOT call create-project again, must NOT ask whether to create another, and must NOT joke, celebrate or use an emoji about it.

transcript.aiResponse:
Added "Book Madrid hotel" for tomorrow. I can also:
- find hotels near the venue
- block time on your calendar
- set a reminder
- create a packing list
Which would you like?

cases.expectation: A reply that creates something. The agent MUST call quick-create-action with a scheduledStart for tomorrow, confirm the action, and end with at most ONE next step (a single question or suggestion) or none. It must NOT end with a menu or list of several offers.

transcript.userMessage: Add an action to visit the Prado on Monday morning.
transcript.aiResponse: Added "Visit the Prado Monday (opens 10am, closed after 2pm, 25 min from hotel)" for Monday.

cases.expectation: Logistics not looked up. No tool in this conversation returned the Prado's opening hours or travel time. The agent MUST create the action with a title carrying only what the user said (e.g. "Visit the Prado", scheduledStart Monday), and any opening-hours or travel remark MUST be hedged in the reply ("usually", "worth checking"). A web search is not needed; if the agent does look the hours up, it may state them in the reply with the source, but the title still carries only what the user asked for. It must NOT write opening hours, closing times, prices or travel times into the action title as constraints.
